secondary_os: Windows 10 where Microsoft guidance still applies
scope.purpose: Machine-readable starter knowledge base for a diagnostic and repair application
scope.coverage_warning: This is broad but not exhaustive. Windows symptoms are many-to-many: one symptom can have several causes and one cause can create several symptoms.

evidence_policy.confirmed: Microsoft release health, Microsoft Support/Learn, or an affected hardware/software vendor documents the issue and remedy.
evidence_policy.supported_general: Microsoft documents the diagnostic or repair path, but it is not proof of a specific root cause.
evidence_policy.watchlist: YouTube, forums, social posts, or technical media supply a signal only. Never use these alone to authorize a privileged or destructive repair.

automation_policy.0_observe: Read-only inventory and diagnostics. Safe default.
automation_policy.1_reversible: Low-impact change with a known reversal. Explain and log it.
automation_policy.2_admin: Administrative repair with prerequisites and post-checks. Require informed consent.
automation_policy.3_disruptive: May remove settings, drivers, updates, or connectivity. Require backup, consent, and rollback plan.
automation_policy.4_manual_only: Boot, partition, firmware, encryption, broad permissions, reset, or reinstall work. Never run unattended.

global_preflight: Identify edition, version, OS build, architecture, device model, firmware version, recent KBs, and recent driver/app changes.
Save user work and confirm a usable backup before any level 2 or higher action.
Confirm the BitLocker recovery key is available before WinRE, boot, firmware, TPM, Secure Boot, or partition changes. Never upload or retain the key.
Check whether the device is organization-managed; defer policy, activation, WSUS, VPN, and security controls to the administrator.
Create a restore point when supported before driver, registry, or update rollback operations.
Run one change at a time, capture before/after evidence, and stop when the symptom is resolved.
never_automate_unattended: Clear TPM, disable Secure Boot, change UEFI/BIOS boot mode, flash firmware, or edit boot entries.
Recursively take ownership of or reset ACLs on Windows, Program Files, Users, or the system drive.
Disable Defender, SmartScreen, firewall, memory integrity, or update services as a permanent fix.
Run debloat, registry-cleaner, driver-updater, or optimizer scripts from videos or download sites.
Remove storage, chipset, network, or display drivers without a verified OEM replacement and recovery path.
Reset Windows, format a drive, or reinstall the OS without explicit consent and verified backup.
Delete update caches, component-store content, restore points, or user profiles as a first-line repair.

issue_families.title: Update files or component store are corrupt or incomplete
diagnostics: Record the exact KB and error
Check free space
Run Windows Update troubleshooter
Inspect CBS.log and generated WindowsUpdate.log when escalation is needed
safe_actions: Use Fix problems using Windows Update to reinstall the current version if available
stop_conditions: DISM reports an unrepaired source error
device is managed by an organization

issue_families.title: Windows Update service is stopped or disabled
symptoms: Updates do not scan or download
diagnostics: Check Windows Update service state
Check whether Group Policy or management owns the setting
safe_actions: Restore the service to its supported configuration when it was changed locally
stop_conditions: Domain, MDM, WSUS, or security policy controls the service
avoid: disabling update services as a performance tweak

issue_families.title: Insufficient free space blocks an update
symptoms: download completes but install cannot continue
diagnostics: Measure OS-volume free space
Distinguish OS-volume shortage from EFI-partition shortage
safe_actions: Use Storage recommendations or Disk Cleanup
Move personal files to backed-up storage

issue_families.title: Feature upgrade fails or rolls back
diagnostics: Read SetupDiagResults.xml
Run current SetupDiag when needed
Prefer the last matched fatal failure
Inspect setupact.log and setuperr.log
safe_actions: Resolve the matched driver, app, storage, or compatibility block
Update from OEM and Windows Update
Retry only after the blocker is removed
stop_conditions: BitLocker or storage filter driver is involved

issue_families.title: Windows system files are damaged
diagnostics: Run DISM health repair before SFC
Record CBS output
Check disk health if corruption returns
safe_actions: Repair reinstall of the current Windows version
stop_conditions: storage or memory errors are present
avoid: Replacing random DLLs from the internet

issue_families.title: Unexpected restart, stop error, BSOD, or black crash screen
diagnostics: Capture stop code and named module
Check recently added hardware or drivers
Check Device Manager
Preserve minidumps
Confirm 10-15% free disk space
safe_actions: Install Windows and OEM driver updates
Use System Restore when timing is clear
avoid: Guessing from the stop-code name alone

issue_families.title: Blank or black screen without a stop code
diagnostics: Separate no-display from BSOD
Check power, cables, input, and alternate monitor
Check whether Ctrl+Alt+Del appears
safe_actions: Press Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B to reset the graphics driver
Restart Windows Explorer from Task Manager
Boot Safe Mode and use an OEM-approved graphics driver
avoid: removing the only graphics driver without a fallback

issue_families.title: Windows does not start
diagnostics: Identify the startup phase
Confirm the disk is detected in firmware
Obtain BitLocker key before WinRE
safe_actions: Use System Restore or uninstall a recent update from WinRE when indicated
stop_conditions: boot configuration differs from standard Windows layout

issue_families.title: BitLocker recovery prompt
diagnostics: Identify recent firmware, hardware, Secure Boot, boot-order, or policy changes
For repeating prompts, inspect Secure Boot and PXE boot configuration with OEM/admin guidance
safe_actions: Retrieve the key from the owner's Microsoft/work/school account or administrator
Install OEM firmware only when a documented fix matches
avoid: changing Secure Boot without device-specific instructions

issue_families.title: Wi-Fi connected but no internet
symptoms: local network works but web does not
diagnostics: Test another device
Check IP, gateway, DNS, proxy, VPN, and router
Distinguish device issue from ISP/router outage
stop_conditions: Static IP, corporate VPN, Hyper-V, or managed network is present
avoid: Changing DNS or proxy without preserving settings

issue_families.title: Persistent network stack or adapter failure
diagnostics: Check physical switch
Check adapter and WLAN AutoConfig
Export network/VPN configuration
Download OEM driver before removal
safe_actions: Use Network reset only as a last supported step
stop_conditions: VPN, virtual switch, static addressing, or enterprise policy is present
avoid: Removing an adapter driver without offline replacement
network reset without warning that adapters and profiles will be rebuilt

issue_families.title: No sound or wrong audio output
diagnostics: Check mute, volume mixer, default output, format, and per-app routing
Test another output
Check Device Manager
safe_actions: Install or roll back the exact OEM audio driver when timing supports it
stop_conditions: device uses vendor DSP or enhancement stack

issue_families.title: Microphone is not detected or apps cannot use it
symptoms: works in one app but not another
diagnostics: Test in Sound settings
Check physical mute
Check device and app privacy permissions
safe_actions: Select and test the correct input
Reinstall/update the exact audio driver if the device is missing
avoid: Granting microphone access to every app

issue_families.title: Bluetooth connects but audio is missing, poor, or unstable
diagnostics: Confirm correct output
Check Bluetooth profile and audio format
Test device elsewhere
stop_conditions: Device firmware or codec limitation is suspected
avoid: Deleting all paired devices without consent

issue_families.title: Print queue is stuck or Print Spooler is not running
diagnostics: Inspect print queue
Check Print Spooler service
Identify duplicate or outdated printer drivers
safe_actions: Install the printer manufacturer's current driver
stop_conditions: specialized label, medical, or industrial printer
avoid: clearing jobs belonging to other users without approval

issue_families.title: Camera missing, busy, blocked, or fails to start
diagnostics: Check physical shutter/switch
Test the Camera app
Check privacy permissions
Check whether another process owns the camera
Inspect Device Manager
stop_conditions: Windows Hello depends on vendor-specific camera extensions
avoid: replacing OEM camera driver without noting Windows Hello impact

issue_families.title: Device Manager reports a device or driver error
diagnostics: Record exact code, hardware ID, driver provider/version, and recent changes
safe_actions: Use the PC or device manufacturer's driver
Roll back only when a recent driver clearly introduced the failure
stop_conditions: Storage, chipset, display, security, or input device is the only working device of its class

issue_families.title: Microsoft Store does not open
diagnostics: Check Windows updates
Check date, time, region, and account state
avoid: Removing Store packages with unofficial PowerShell scripts

issue_families.title: Desktop or Store app will not install, uninstall, update, or open
diagnostics: Identify Store versus desktop installer
Check free space and malware status
Check whether repair/reset is supported
safe_actions: Use app Reset only after warning about local app data
stop_conditions: app is managed or licensed by an organization

issue_families.title: Windows activation fails
diagnostics: Check edition, license channel, date/time, network, recent motherboard change, and organization ownership
safe_actions: Sign in with the Microsoft account linked to the digital license
Contact OEM, reseller, organization, or Microsoft as the code requires

issue_families.title: OneDrive cannot sign in, connect, or finish syncing
diagnostics: Check service status and web access
Confirm personal versus work/school account
Check open, very large, invalid, or blocked files
Check storage quota
safe_actions: Unlink/relink only after confirming cloud copies and account identity
Use the documented OneDrive reset for matching errors
stop_conditions: PST/OST or organization retention policy is involved

issue_families.title: File Explorer will not open, freezes, or crashes
diagnostics: Restart Explorer and observe
Check Event Viewer for explorer.exe crash
Test Safe Mode or clean boot
Correlate with recent shell-extension or update installation
stop_conditions: User profile corruption or storage errors are suspected
enterprise XAML provisioning issue matches KB5072911
avoid: third-party shell-extension tools as an automatic first step

issue_families.title: Explorer, Start, Settings, Taskbar, or Search fail on some provisioned enterprise devices
diagnostics: Confirm enterprise provisioning scenario and affected update path
Check XAML package registration and relevant event logs
safe_actions: Use Microsoft's KB5072911 enterprise remediation exactly as documented
Deploy through the organization's supported management process
avoid: Running package-registration commands generically on every shell problem

issue_families.title: Battery drain, poor standby, or unexpected wake
diagnostics: Generate powercfg /batteryreport
On Modern Standby devices generate powercfg /sleepstudy
Check recent drivers, active devices, and battery health
stop_conditions: Battery swelling, overheating, or hardware failure is possible
avoid: firmware updates without AC power and model match

issue_families.title: Malware or unwanted software is suspected
diagnostics: Check Windows Security protection history and update definitions
Preserve evidence on managed or business devices
safe_actions: Use Microsoft Defender Offline for persistent threats
Escalate suspected credential theft or ransomware
stop_conditions: Ransomware, credential theft, business compromise, or repeated reinfection
avoid: uploading sensitive files to unknown scanners

issue_families.title: Dell Intel Innovation Platform Framework incompatibility
diagnostics: Confirm affected Dell model and installed KB/build
safe_actions: Install KB5121767 when Windows Update offers it to the affected device
avoid: Installing the OOB update on unrelated devices as a generic performance fix

issue_families.title: May 2026 update fails near 35-36 percent because EFI free space is 10 MB or less
diagnostics: Confirm the specific May 2026 issue and EFI free-space condition
safe_actions: Allow Known Issue Rollback to apply where relevant
avoid: registry workaround without expert review and backup

issue_families.title: USB keyboard and mouse unavailable in Windows Recovery Environment
symptoms: USB input works in Windows but not WinRE
diagnostics: Confirm October 2025 affected update path
safe_actions: If locked out use touchscreen, PS/2, recovery media, or enterprise PXE/WinPE

issue_families.title: Cloud-backed file operations hang apps, including classic Outlook PST on OneDrive
diagnostics: Confirm January 2026 update timing and cloud-backed/PST location
safe_actions: Move PST only with Microsoft's documented procedure
stop_conditions: Unsynced mail data or retention requirements
avoid: Moving or deleting PST/OST files automatically

issue_families.title: Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 credential prompts fail
diagnostics: Confirm Windows App client and January 2026 update timing
safe_actions: Use supported Remote Desktop or web client temporarily
stop_conditions: Conditional Access or organization policy may be the cause

issue_families.title: Samsung Galaxy Connect or Continuity causes C drive access denied
diagnostics: Confirm an affected Galaxy Book 4/Desktop model and Samsung software state
safe_actions: Follow the joint Microsoft/Samsung model-specific recovery guidance
Contact Samsung support when recovery does not match
avoid: takeown/icacls recursion on the system drive

issue_families.title: WSUS synchronization slows or times out from publishing metadata buildup
diagnostics: Confirm WSUS role and server history
Check current Microsoft release-health status
safe_actions: New or rebuilt servers need no special action after the July 18 mitigation
Wait for Microsoft's cleanup guidance for previously affected servers
stop_conditions: Server was already affected before mitigation

issue_families.title: Display tint, black screen, or monitor behavior reported after July 2026 updates
diagnostics: Record GPU, monitor, cable, color profile, driver, OS build, and KB
Test whether Safe Mode or another monitor reproduces it
safe_actions: Use only OEM/GPU-vendor approved driver update or rollback
Report a reproducible trace through Feedback Hub
stop_conditions: No clear update timing or reproduction
avoid: monitor/GPU firmware flash without model-specific vendor guidance

issue_families.title: Windows Hello face, fingerprint, or PIN sign-in fails
diagnostics: Confirm an alternate sign-in method works
Check camera/fingerprint hardware and privacy state
Check Windows, firmware, and biometric drivers
Identify organization anti-spoofing or sign-in policy
safe_actions: Clean the sensor and improve recognition
Reset the PIN through the supported account flow
avoid: Deleting the NGC folder or credential data as a generic fix
disabling enhanced sign-in security without explaining the security reduction

issue_families.title: Remote Desktop cannot connect or is disconnected
symptoms: Unable to connect to Remote Desktop
diagnostics: Test reachability and the exact port
Confirm host edition and Remote Desktop enablement
Check account authorization, session limits, authentication, encryption, certificate, firewall, VPN, and time
Collect supported traces before changing policy
safe_actions: Correct the confirmed reachability, authorization, certificate, or service issue
Use an approved web/client alternative while the organization investigates
stop_conditions: Conditional Access, gateway, certificate, or domain policy is involved

issue_families.title: USB-C, USB4, Thunderbolt, dock, display, charging, or device recognition failure
error_codes: Device Manager codes except Code 28 require code-specific handling
diagnostics: Record the Device Manager code
Verify the port, cable, dock, charger, power rating, Alternate Mode, and USB4/Thunderbolt support
Test direct connection without a hub
safe_actions: Use the manufacturer-provided or certified cable/charger
Connect to the correct supported port
Install OEM dock, chipset, USB, and firmware updates when model-specific
stop_conditions: device supplies power to the PC
avoid: Assuming every USB-C cable supports charging, video, and USB4
firmware flashing without exact model/power prerequisites

issue_families.title: User profile is corrupted
symptoms: problem follows one user but not another
diagnostics: Verify the issue is profile-specific with a separate test account
Back up user data
Inventory mail data, encryption, app state, and cloud-sync status
safe_actions: Sign in and copy supported user files
stop_conditions: domain profile, FSLogix, or enterprise profile management
avoid: deleting the old profile before verification
registry ProfileList edits as a generic repair

issue_families.title: Low storage, storage health warning, or recurring disk-related failures
diagnostics: Check Storage and Windows Security Device performance & health
Record free space and device health
Back up first when hardware failure is plausible
safe_actions: Use Windows drive optimization appropriate to HDD or SSD
Escalate hardware warnings to the OEM or storage vendor
avoid: Stress-testing a failing drive before backup
running chkdsk /f automatically on a suspect drive without a recovery plan

issue_families.title: Game crashes, stutters, or has DirectX/audio/video problems
diagnostics: Capture dxdiag and game logs
Record GPU driver, refresh/HDR state, overlays, anti-cheat, temperatures, and whether other games reproduce
Separate network latency from frame-time stutter
safe_actions: Verify game files using the official launcher
Use vendor-specific hotfix or rollback only when the exact issue is documented
avoid: installing DirectX DLL packs from websites
